description: Validator for JavaScript and TypeScript with rules that are just data (Language Independent Validation Rules): sync and async validators, custom rules and aliases, TypeScript types inferred from the schema, zero dependencies.
rules: A schema is plain data: { field: rules }, where rules are a rule name ('required'), a rule with arguments ({ min_length: 8 }) or a list of them. Rule names work in snake_case and camelCase

import LIVR from 'livr': new LIVR.Validator(schema).validate(data) returns the validated data, or false and the errors in validator.getErrors(). import LIVR from 'livr/async': new LIVR.AsyncValidator(schema).validate(data) returns a promise that rejects with the errors
TypeScript: write the schema as const and get the type with InferFromSchema<typeof schema> from 'livr/types'
Prefer an alias (registerAliasedRule(), existing rules under a new name and error code) to a rule function when existing rules can do the check

A rule function (registerRules()) gets the rule arguments and returns (value, allValues, outputArr) => errorCode | undefined. It skips empty values (undefined, null, '') and pushes to outputArr to change the value. registerDefaultRules() and registerAliasedDefaultRule() register rules for all validators

Registering a rule does not give it a type. Declare the type of every custom rule and alias in RuleTypes with declare module 'livr/types/inference', in a .ts file with an import or an export: As<T>, a plain type, AliasType<typeof rules> or an interface that extends RuleType
